question: Which statement best describes <label> association (for/id and wrapping)?
options: <textarea> captures multi-line input; unlike <input>, its value is the text between its tags, not a value attribute. rows and cols set the visible size, maxlength caps length, and CSS resize controls user resizing. It's used for messages, comments, and descriptions where a single-line field is insufficient.

<select> is a dropdown of <option> elements; the option's value (or its text if no value) is submitted under the select's name. Add selected to set a default, multiple to allow several choices (becomes a list box), and size to show more than one row. A common pattern is a disabled placeholder option as the first entry.

A label names a control programmatically. Two ways to associate them: explicit, where label's for matches the control's id; or implicit, where the control sits inside the label. Either makes the label clickable to focus the control and lets screen readers announce the control's name. Every control needs a label.

<optgroup> groups related <option>s under a non-selectable label, useful for long lists like countries-by-continent or fonts-by-category. The label attribute provides the group heading. It purely organizes the dropdown visually and semantically; the submitted value is still the chosen option's value.
